pid_file.description: Path where Perlbal writes its process ID (PID) file.

enable_ssl.description: If enabled, Perlbal will attempt to use TLS/SSL for incoming and/or outgoing connections. Requires valid ssl_cert and ssl_key.

ssl_cert.description: Path to the SSL certificate file (PEM format). Only used if enable_ssl is true.

ssl_key.description: Path to the SSL private key file (PEM format). Only used if enable_ssl is true.

services.description: List of services (reverse proxies or web servers) to configure. Each defines a named Perlbal service instance.

name.description: Unique name of the Perlbal service (used in CREATE/ENABLE directives).

description.description: Human-readable description of the service (for documentation only).

role.description: Role of the service — typically 'reverse_proxy' or 'web_server'.

listen_ip.description: IP address the service should bind to (e.g., 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0, or specific interface IP).

listen_port.description: Port number the service listens on.

pool_size.description: Maximum number of concurrent connections to the backend pool.

backends.description: List of backend servers to balance traffic across.

host.description: Hostname or IP address of the backend server.

port.description: Port on which the backend service listens.

weight.description: Relative weight for load distribution (higher = more traffic).

status.description: Whether the backend is 'enabled' or 'disabled'. Disabled backends are omitted from the ADD directive.

health_check_interval.description: Interval (in seconds) between health checks. Set to 0 or omit to disable.

health_check_path.description: Path used for HTTP health checks (e.g., /health or /ping).

max_connections.description: Maximum number of concurrent client connections Perlbal will accept for this service.

client_timeout.description: Idle timeout (in seconds) for client connections.

server_timeout.description: Idle timeout (in seconds) for backend server connections.

vhost.description: Virtual hostname this service responds to (used for Host-header-based routing).
